statement: The collinear-centre case is treated by new quadratic equations. For a common radical axis, pairs collapse to the two common intersection points; special similarity-centre alignments produce two common tangent lines with six other generic solutions.

source.location: Equations (35)–(41) and following discussion, original pp.627–632, especially pp.630–632
source.version: Original German journal article (1873), GDZ article scan; PDF page 1 is a digitization cover, original p.613 begins on PDF page 2.

scope: Special input configurations with collinear centres or a common radical axis; ordinary admissible circles distinguished from zero-radius and infinite-radius limiting solutions.
notes: This analyses completed limiting objects and failure of the generic elimination chart; it does not say every collinear-centre input has fewer ordinary solutions or an infinite fibre. Migration: Merge exceptional-fibre behaviour into Exceptional locus; preserve each source result separately.
